Both test claims carry p as 0.0000000000 with display_digits 4, so a surface will render p as 0.0000; the release should render it as p below 0.0001 (the recomputed p is about 3e-157 for completion and underflows to zero for AOV), not as a p of exactly zero.

Both test claims name bonferroni with alpha 0.05 but do not state the adjusted per-test alpha (0.025 for the two registered tests); the conclusion is unaffected because both p values are far below any corrected threshold.

claims_recomputed (rooted in raw_data via raw_latest) covers only the six point and estimate claims; the two test claims are recomputed by recompute_test from clean_data, so their only path back to the source is this auditor's recalc from quarantine/orders.csv, which agrees.

The completion-rate gap between channels is observational: it holds with the same sign in every country and every month of the quarter (about 0.10 to 0.13), but nothing in the export identifies why partner orders complete less often, and no claim should be read as causal.
summary: All eight claims recompute independently from quarantine/orders.csv (last revision per order_id, Q1 by order_month, negative refunds excluded: 44531 orders) and the claim->metric->source chain is byte-equal for every value, bound, n, level, method, statistic, effect and p; plan, groups, alpha and correction match audit/analysis_plan.json; no Simpson reversal or confounding by country or month.
